title: Tech Note: 4D and The Internet, An Overview
author: David Adams
featured_technology: Third-party 4D Internet toolkits (ITK, PDM Internet Tools, TCP ToolKit)

historical_commentary.text: This note is a broad 1996 overview/roadmap of how 4D could participate in the still-young Web/Internet — as a CGI via AppleEvents, as a page-management/database-publishing tool, as an Internet client, or as a full Web/FTP/mail server built with third-party TCP toolkits — referencing a landscape of now-defunct products (WebSTAR, NetLink/4D, ITK, NetWings, Web Server 4D) and pre-Web-standard practices; the specific products and CGI-via-AppleEvents architecture are entirely obsolete, but the note's framing of database-driven dynamic web content and Internet-client integration reflects a still-relevant idea that 4D (like any database) can be a powerful engine behind web-facing systems.
related_updates: 4D gained a built-in web server and 4D Internet Commands plugin around 1997-1998, replacing the third-party AppleEvent/CGI approach (NetLink/4D, WebSTAR, System 7 Pack) described here
Virtually all of the named third-party products (NetLink/4D, NetWings, Web Server 4D, ITK, PDM Internet Tools, TCP ToolKit, WebSTAR, MacHTTP) are long discontinued
Modern 4D web development uses ORDA and REST APIs, not CGI/AppleEvent bridging to an external web server
